free_tier.stated: No published byte quota, and the empirical evidence points to a tight request-body limit rather than a documented number: a 2,072,566-byte distribution was rejected with 'Upload failed (request failed with error code 413 Message: Request Entity Too Large)' in April 2024, and the same upload succeeded shortly after, so the 413 was transient rather than a hard 2 MB cap. Treat the ceiling as a few MB, undocumented.

retention.stated: per-object-cap: undocumented; 413s observed around 2 MB, transient. retention: permanent and immutable per version

egress.terms: Free and globally mirrored (CPAN mirror ring); no metering.

tooling: `cpan-upload` / `pause upload` (HTTP POST to pause.perl.org/pause/authenquery?ACTION=add_uri), plus the historical FTP path. Read side is plain HTTP from any CPAN mirror.
chaining: unlimited distributions x unlimited versions, but each must be a valid Perl distribution tarball with a version number in the filename, and 'you will never be able to upload a file with identical' name+version. Cardinality is real; size per unit is tiny.

extras.agent_focus: The code-forge seam: OSS project hosts, software-download directories, game/mod distribution and mirror services. Question for each: (a) any published byte quota, (b) is upload possible over SFTP/rsync/SCP/SSH rather than a web form, (c) is there a public download CDN, (d) does it need an approved project or can any account create one, (e) per-file cap. Round 2 flagged that SourceForge has no published quota and serves over plain SFTP with a global mirror CDN, and that an rclone-backend enumerator would score the niche as empty. This slot tests that class systematically. Every number below was read live or from a dated archive capture this session.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
